Definition: from the same as G188; to make a point, i.e. (figuratively) mature:--be fully ripe.
BiblicalUsage: Once, in the vision of the harvest: an angel cries to the one with the sharp sickle, Thrust in thy sharp sickle, and gather the clusters of the vine of the earth; for her grapes are fully ripe. The word is ripeness at its peak — the moment when the fruit can wait no longer, and the harvest must come.
TheologicalSignificance: One word for fully ripe carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the harvest vision, where evil ripens like grapes and judgment comes at exactly the right time.
RelatedTopics: Judgment; Day of the Lord; End Times
